1. 로마서의 기록 목적\n - 바울이 마지막으로 예루살렘에 가기 위해서:
1. Why Romans was written
 - When Paul had collected the offering to go up to Jerusalem for the last time and was staying in Greece for three months, he wrote Romans and sent it to Rome in the hands of a sister named Phoebe, a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.
로마서는 여집사가 읽어주고 설명해 줄 정도로 쉽게 써진 것인데 오늘날 신:
Romans was written simply enough that a woman deacon could read it out and explain it, but today's theologians have made it hard. Truth is simple to begin with. This isn't a theology paper; it's a letter. Back then, a sister named Phoebe would read it out, they'd ask a few questions, and everybody understood it. That's what annoys me most about theologians. These people have a talent for explaining easy things in a hard way.
 1) To give them a head start on the gospel Paul preaches
 - He was going to visit Rome, and if he sent Romans ahead of time, then when Paul got there, things could move along efficiently.
 2) So that the gospel would get there even if he couldn't
 - Paul had tried hard many times to go to Rome, but strangely it never worked out and he couldn't go. Even now he wasn't sure whether he'd make it to Rome or not, so if he did go, this would prepare them ahead of time, and if he didn't, he wrote it thinking the gospel still had to get there.
2. 로마서의 내용\n 1) 로마서를 쓰게 된 동기, 방문 계획, 문안:
2. What Romans says
 1) Why he wrote Romans, his plans to visit, greetings, explaining the theme, and so on (1:1~1:17)
 2) The sins of the people God gives up (1:18~1:32)
<롬1:24~32> 그러므로 하나님께서 저희를 마음의 정욕대로 더러움에:
<Rom 1:24~32> Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves; who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen. For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature. Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error. Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting; being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers, backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unmerciful; who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.
 - It keeps saying he gave them up, gave them up... but rather than ‘God actively abandoned them,’ we should understand it as the result of the fact that God doesn't force people who do evil even though they know it's wrong.
- God gave us free will, but when we misuse it, God leaves us to it. Because that's what freedom is... If he stepped in every time things went wrong, it wouldn't be freedom.
- With the children he has chosen, he does step in. He means to teach them even if it takes a spanking, but he doesn't spank just anyone.
 3) Chapter 2, a word to the Jews - What matters isn't having the law but whether you do it
<롬2:1~2> 그러므로 남을 판단하는 사람아 무론 누구든지 네가 핑계치:
<Rom 2:1~2> Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things. We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.
 - Even while calling yourself a Jew, you can very well commit the sin of rebelling against God.
Verse 13: Before God it's not the hearers of the law who are righteous but the doers.
Being circumcised physically doesn't make it count; you have to be circumcised in your heart. The law engraved on the heart. It's a sharp rebuke to the Jews who were showing off just because they had the mark.
 4) Everyone is a sinner before God. (chapter 3)
 - The Jews do have an advantage. They were entrusted with the word of God.
의로우신 이는 하나님 밖에 없기 때문에 어떤 사람이 믿든지 안 믿든지 하: Only God is righteous, so whether anyone believes or not, God's righteousness doesn't change.
<롬3:9~12> 그러면 어떠하뇨 우리는 나으뇨 결코 아니라 유대인이나:
<Rom 3:9~12> What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we previously warned both Jews and Greeks, that they are all under sin. As it is written, “There is no one righteous; no, not one. There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks after God. They have all turned away. They have together become unprofitable. There is no one who does good, no, not, so much as one.”
 - So we can't keep the law perfectly. And anyway, being declared righteous doesn't come by doing the law. In other words, the law's job was never to make us righteous in the first place, but to make us realize what is sin and what isn't.
그렇다면....\n 5) 어떻게 하나님 앞에서 우리가 의롭다 함을 받을:
Then....
 5) How can we be declared righteous before God? We are declared righteous by faith. Justification (chapter 4)
<롬4:3> 성경이 무엇을 말하느뇨 아브라함이 하나님을 믿으매 이것이 저:
<Rom 4:3> For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”
 - The point is that the moment Abraham was declared righteous was before he was circumcised, in other words, ‘before keeping the rules of the law, he was declared righteous because he believed God.’
 - Works VS faith, it looks like they clash, but....
 - The faith talked about here is faith that shows itself in works. But the Jews kept the law as a formality and thought that doing so had some power in itself.
 - Faith is the condition and works are the result. Works are not the condition. Jesus said you can know people by their fruit.
31절 그런즉 우리가 믿음으로 말미암아 율법을 파기하는냐 그럴 수 없느니:
Verse 31: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! No, we establish the law. - People who believe actually end up establishing the law firmly.
 6) Once you're declared righteous... now you have to grow until you're at peace with God. (chapter 5)
<롬5:1> 그러므로 우리가 믿음으로 의롭다 하심을 얻었은즉 우리 주 예:
<Rom 5:1> Being therefore justified by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
 - It doesn't end with being forgiven and declared righteous; you have to go on into being at peace with God.
그리스도를 통해서 가능하다. => 대표성의 원리를 설명 => 아담은 인간: It's possible through Christ. => He explains the principle of representation => Adam stands for all humanity
즉, 아담 = 인간, 아담이 죄인이 되었다는 것은 인간의 존재가 죄인로: In other words, Adam = humanity; Adam becoming a sinner means human existence itself was changed into a sinner.
한 사람이 범죄 함으로 이런 일이 일어 났으니 한 사람의 희생으로 모든: Since this happened because one man sinned, through the sacrifice of one man everyone can receive life
17절 한 사람의 범죄로 말미암아 사망이 그 한 사람을 통하여 왕 노릇: Verse 17: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; so much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
18절 그런즉 한 범죄로 많은 사람이 정죄에 이른 것 같이 한 의로운 행:
Verse 18: So then as through one trespass many people came to condemnation, even so through one act of righteousness many people were justified and came to life.
 7) How serious original sin is (chapters 6~7)
 - If we've received such huge benefits, we shouldn't be slaves to sin anymore, and yet people keep on sinning, right? This is what we call the sinful nature. E.g.> inertia => a tendency that keeps pulling us to sin
-The writer of Proverbs says if a person knows to do good and doesn't do it, that's sin.
말하자면 우리 상태가 마이너스예요. 0도 아니고 마이너스. 죄 쪽으로 가:
So to put it another way, our condition is in the minus. Not even zero, minus. We have a tendency to drift toward sin, so what do we have to do? Only by working hard at doing good can we barely stay where we are. That's our situation.
 - So how should we go about trying to do good?
12절 그러므로 너희는 죄가 너희 죽을 몸을 지배하지 못하게 하여 몸의:
Verse 12: Therefore don't let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts. Verse 13: Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God. If you do that... verse 14: For sin will not have dominion over you. For you are not under law, but under grace.
- So since we're under grace, can we live however we want? No, as people who've received grace, we should live even more righteously.
7장에 가면 율법의 시효에 대해서 비유를 합니다.\n- 법이라는 것은 사:
In chapter 7 he uses an illustration about how long the law stays in force.
- The law is in force while a person is alive, but once they're dead, it's ‘case closed, no right to prosecute,’ and they don't charge them anymore, right? When Christ died, we died with him. So the law has nothing to do with us who are dead. So now we're not to live by the letter of the law but in the newness of the Spirit.
 - But the sin inside us, what kind of state does it put us in? Verse 22: For I delight in God's law after the inward person, verse 23: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
- You're like that too, right? You do delight in God's law, but when it comes to actually doing it, it doesn't go so well, does it?
- So Paul sighs too. What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?
 8) The way to be set free from original sin (chapter 8)
<롬8:1~2> 그러므로 이제 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 자에게는 결코 정:
<Rom 8:1~2> There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made you free from the law of sin and of death.
 - Jesus has prepared the way like this.
 - Verse 3: What we can't do because our flesh is weak, God does.
어떻게? 자기 아들을 대신 죽이심으로 율법의 요구를 충족하셨다. 죄의 삯:
How? He met the law's demand by having his own Son die in our place. The wages of sin being death...
 - The law demands death as the price for breaking the law, and Jesus paid that demand by dying in our place. If someone ate it for you, it's eaten, right? If someone paid it for you, it's paid, right? If someone died for you? Then it's died. That's what redemption, a death in our place, is. Because he redeemed us, we've become free with regard to the law.
 - Because he paid in our place, we're all debtors. => Verse 12: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh. => If someone died because of my wrongdoing, then if I have any conscience at all, I can't repeat that wrong again.
- If you live with this heart of a debtor, you can overcome the sinful nature. But we can't do it in our own strength; we need to be led by the Holy Spirit. Those who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God, and if you're a son, you're given the right to inherit, but to receive this glory... the second half of verse 17: if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
기독교는 복음과 함께 고난을 받는 것. 복 받는 것은 나중 얘기고. 예수: Christianity is suffering together with the gospel. Being blessed comes later. He says that anyone who confesses Jesus as Lord will surely have suffering.
But don't worry too much. The Holy Spirit helps us in our weakness. He even prays for us.... Is it only the Holy Spirit? Look at verse 34. Who else? Jesus also intercedes for us. And look at verse 31. Everyone, if God is for us, who can be against us?
그러니까 걱정 말아라 37-39절 이 모든 일에 우리를 사랑하시는 이로:
So don't worry. Verses 37-39: No, in all these things, we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. Can I get an amen?
 9) Paul's aching heart for the Jewish people (chapter 9)
<롬9:1~3> 내가 그리스도 안에서 참말을 하고 거짓말을 아니하노라 내:
<Rom 9:1~3> I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit (this is part of verse 1) that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers' sake, my relatives according to the flesh.
 - Paul loves his own people so much that he wants the Jews to be saved even if he himself is cut off from Christ.
- From verse 30 on, what he's saying is: God gave them the law, but they couldn't keep it well and were struggling, so God paid an enormous price, the life of his only Son, and wiped it all away as if it never happened. That's the good news, and the Gentiles heard this good news early on and received righteousness. But the Jews are still sweating blood trying to keep the law.
왜 그러냐? 자신들의 잘 되지도 않는 행위를 가지고 어찌 해보려고 하니까:
Why is that? Because they're trying to make it work with their own works that don't even work.... Look at chapter 10 verse 3. For being ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they didn't subject themselves to the righteousness of God. So from where Paul stands, it's heartbreaking.
 10) (chapter 10)
그래서 10장에 보면 그런 열심은 참 지식에 근거한 열심히 아니라서 효력: So in chapter 10 he says that kind of zeal isn't zeal based on true knowledge, so it has no effect. Then what to do for these Jews is Paul's homework.
그래서 11장 1절 보시면 하나님께서 유대인들을 버리신게 아니라고 말합니:
So if you look at chapter 11 verse 1, he says God hasn't rejected the Jews.
 11) God's plan for the final salvation of the Jews (chapter 11)
 - Paul quietly watches how things are going, and God seems to be leaving the Jews out in the cold and pouring out grace on the Gentiles, right? So he realizes, ‘Aha! He's doing this to make the Jews jealous!’ What I mean is, God gave us free will. So God doesn't do things by force. So there's a way he can do something without damaging our freedom, and that's jealousy.
 - Like, for example, when Seon-ju was a baby. She was a good eater, but sometimes she'd say she wasn't going to eat. And this little one has a will too, so you can't force the spoon into her mouth, right? So what do you do then? ‘If you don't eat this, I'll give it to Jun-yeol~’ She comes right over and eats.
 - Once Paul realized God had chosen this method, he said, ‘I was sent to the Gentiles. Just as God called Peter as the apostle to the Jews, he called me as the apostle to the Gentiles,’ and threw himself into the mission to the Gentiles. Why? Because only when the Gentiles are happily eating and enjoying themselves will the Jews get jealous, and then finally come saying ‘I want some too’....
하나님 입장에서는 손 안대고 코푸는거죠. 유대인도 구원하고, 열혈청년 바:
From God's point of view, it's like blowing your nose without using your hands, getting it done without lifting a finger. He saves the Jews, and by using Paul, that passionate young man, he saves the Gentiles too.... That's why Paul marvels. Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!
- And then he warns the Gentiles. You're as good as saved out of death. A grafted-in branch had better not get cocky. God is the kind of God who will cut off even the natural branches if they go wrong. He says that too.
12장부터는 ‘그러므로’ 하면서 실천편 입니다.\n 12) 실천에 앞서:
From chapter 12, with ‘Therefore,’ comes the practical section.
 12) A call to dedication before putting it into practice (chapter 12)
 -
<롬12:1~2> 그러므로 형제들아 내가 하나님의 모든 자비하심으로 너희:
<Rom 12:1~2> Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service. Don't be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
 - Dedication means devoting our lives completely, forever, once for all, wholly and completely. And people who are dedicated must not be conformed to this world.
- Don't be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. You can't overcome evil with a bigger evil.
 13) Civic ethics for believers (chapter 13)
- Submit to the authorities of the world. Do your duty as a citizen. Pay your taxes honestly, do your military service...
- Love is the fulfillment of the law. Adultery, murder, stealing, if you love, these are sins you can't commit.
- The day the Lord comes is not far off. Don't live in reveling, drunkenness, sexual immorality, lustful acts, strife, and jealousy, but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts
 14) Caring for those who are weaker (chapter 14)
<롬14:1> 믿음이 연약한 자를 너희가 받되 그의 의심하는 바를 비판하: <Rom 14:1> Receive the one who is weak in faith, but don't criticize his doubts.
3절 후반에 보면 왜 그래야 하느냐? 너는 못 받아들일지 몰라도 하나님은:
At the end of verse 3, why do we have to do that? Because even if you can't accept him, God has accepted him. There's a saying that honest doubt is better than false faith. Doubt isn't a bad thing. It can be a heart that wants to believe more surely, right?
 - Then he keeps talking about food, for example the question of whether you can eat meat that was offered to idols... Look at verse 15. Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Don't destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
 - This isn't just about food. There are a lot of things we came to understand first, right? He's saying we mustn't use them to tie other people up. You should look at yourself first and work hard at keeping it yourself.... Taking a huge ruler, a huge ruler you can hardly lift yourself, you mustn't keep holding it up against other people. Look at verse 16. If we don't do it that way, our good will be spoken of as evil. The Kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
 15) Let's bear the weaknesses of the weak (chapter 15)
<롬15:1> 우리 강한 자가 마땅히 연약한 자의 약점을 담당하고 자기를:
<Rom 15:1> Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
 - In the church there are strong people and weak people. The reason he made the strong strong is so they'd take care of the weak. Not so they could show off and act big. I told you, if we don't realize this, no matter how much good we do, we'll be criticized, right?
16) Greetings and farewells (chapter 16)
 - Of the 24 people Paul greets, 13 are either royalty or nobility. Paul may not have been much to look at, but this man's scale is so big no one can keep up with it.
 - He closes the letter by giving glory to God.
How about it? Is Romans hard? Explain it this much and read it, and that's all you need.
